svg.text: Numbers show the sequence of royal seats, not a journey or road
1 Ashur: earlier royal seat and enduring religious centre.
2 Kalhu: court established under Ashurnasirpal II in the ninth century BC.
3 Dur-Sharrukin: Sargon II moved the court here in 706 BC.
4 Nineveh: Sennacherib moved the court here after Sargon’s death in 705 BC.
Geographic context • generalised rivers and modern relief; no imperial boundary or campaign route implied.
Terrain / rivers: Sémhur, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0), adapted. Sites: ORACC, UNESCO, Syriaca. Review v01.
